name: Prime Number Check
description: Determines if a number is prime by trial division up to √n. Efficient enough for numbers up to ~10^12.
aim: Check primality by testing divisibility from 2 to √n. If no divisor found, the number is prime.
howItWorks: Handle edge cases: n<2 = not prime
If n=2: prime; if n even: not prime
Check divisors from 3 to √n, step by 2 (skip evens)
If loop ends without divisor: prime

time.worstCase: n is prime or odd composite near √n

realWorld: RSA key generation — needs large primes
Hashing table size selection (prime table sizes reduce collisions)
whenToUse: n is not extremely large (up to ~10^12)
alternatives: Miller-Rabin — probabilistic O(k log² n), good for large primes
Sieve of Eratosthenes — O(n log log n) for all primes up to n
